spec.description:
Peak PCIe MB/s per 30-second capture window.

Tens of MB/s peaks → Normal bursty pattern.

100-500 MB/s peaks → Big market event or reconnect.

>1 GB/s peaks → Investigate — retransmit storm or measurement anomaly.

Typical peak/avg ratio: 7-15×. Ratio >30× consistently → protocol backing up.

panels.description:
Total memory read + write bandwidth in MB/s.

"<2 GB/s" → Normal for HFT (working set fits in cache).

"2-10 GB/s" → Elevated. Investigate what changed.

">10 GB/s" sustained → Memory streaming workload — allocation storm, big scan, or serialization.

">50 GB/s" → Approaching bandwidth wall; latency will suffer.

Sudden step-changes are the anomaly signal. Steady state at any level is fine.

targets.query: SELECT mean("total_avg") AS "total_avg", mean("read_avg") AS "read_avg", mean("write_avg") AS "write_avg" FROM "pcm_memory" WHERE ("scope" = 'system' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(null)

panels.title: System memory bandwidth (MB/s)

panels.description:
Read bandwidth for each of 12 memory channels over time.

Uniform stripes across all channels → Balanced memory allocation.

Consistent bright/dark tier pattern → Normal (NUMA-aware allocator preferring some channels).

Sudden pattern shift → NUMA rebalancing or memory pressure — investigate.

Vertical dark gap → Shipper missed a capture cycle.

targets.query: SELECT mean("read_avg") FROM "pcm_memory" WHERE ("scope" = 'channel' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "channel" fill(previous)

panels.title: Per-channel read bandwidth (heatmap)

panels.description:
Instructions Per Cycle per trading core (filtered by role=trading). Direct measure of core execution efficiency.

IPC 2.5-2.9 → Excellent. Optimized compute code (strategy, decision-making).

IPC 1.5-2.5 → Normal for network-ingest / feed-handler threads (memory-bound reads limit IPC).

IPC 1.0-1.5 → Suspicious for compute cores; normal for spinning/polling threads.

IPC <0.5 → Effectively idle or heavily stalled.

Interpret by thread type — identify with sudo pmu-core-explain <core>.

When to act: A core that was 2.7 dropping to 1.4 = real regression. Look at MPKI/L3 misses next.

targets.query: SELECT mean("ipc_avg") FROM "pcm_numa" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'trading' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/ ) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "core" fill(null)

panels.title: IPC — trading cores (role=trading)

panels.description:
IPC on non-isolated cores (kernel, systemd, monitoring, IRQs).

IPC 0.2-0.7 → Normal. Kernel code is inherently cache-unfriendly.

IPC <0.2 → Very idle.

IPC >1.0 → UNUSUAL. Application workload may have leaked here — check core pinning.

IPC >2.0 → Definite misconfiguration. Trading-quality thread running on housekeeping core.

When to act: Sudden IPC jump on a housekeeping core → workload landed where it shouldn't. 

Identify with sudo pmu-core-explain <core>.

targets.query: SELECT mean("ipc_avg") FROM "pcm_numa" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'housekeeping' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/ ) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "core" fill(null)

panels.title: IPC — housekeeping cores (role=housekeeping)

panels.description:
Fleet averages across all cores including idle ones — naturally lower than hot-core IPC.

IPC 1.0-1.5 → Healthy trading host with active workload.

IPC <0.8 → Host unusually idle. Verify strategies are running.

IPC >2.0 → Every core doing real work — highly saturated.

Cross-host comparison is misleading (48-core vs 96-core naturally differ). Use per-host baseline.

targets.query: SELECT last("ipc_avg") AS "ipc_avg", last("total_instructions_avg") AS "total_instructions_avg" FROM "pcm_numa" WHERE ("scope" = 'system' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "host" fill(null)

panels.title: System-wide IPC & instructions/sec

panels.description:
PCIe device-initiated traffic converted to MB/s (64B cache lines).

PCIRdCur = device reads memory (NIC RX, disk read).

ItoM = device writes memory (NIC TX, disk write).

ItoMCacheNear / WCiLF = coherent cache-line writes.

<10 MB/s avg normal for HFT. >500 MB/s investigate — market data storm or NIC issue.

targets.query: SELECT mean("mbps_avg") FROM "pcm_pcie" WHERE ("metric_kind" = 'mbps' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/ AND ("event" = 'PCIRdCur' OR "event" = 'ItoM' OR "event" = 'ItoMCacheNear' OR "event" = 'WCiLF')) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "event" fill(null)

panels.title: PCIe bandwidth (MB/s, avg per interval)

panels.description:
Peak PCIe MB/s per 30-second capture window.

Tens of MB/s peaks → Normal bursty pattern.

100-500 MB/s peaks → Big market event or reconnect.

">1 GB/s peaks" → Investigate — retransmit storm or measurement anomaly.

Typical peak/avg ratio: 7-15×. Ratio >30× consistently → protocol backing up.

targets.query: SELECT mean("mbps_max") FROM "pcm_pcie" WHERE ("metric_kind" = 'mbps' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/ AND ("event" = 'PCIRdCur' OR "event" = 'ItoM' OR "event" = 'ItoMCacheNear' OR "event" = 'WCiLF')) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "event" fill(null)

panels.title: PCIe peak MB/s per interval

panels.description:
Absolute L3 cache misses per second per trading core. Scales with workload volume, so cross-core comparison is misleading — use MPKI panel below for the true health signal.

Normal outliers (not anomalies): Network-ingest threads (NetworkRead, market_feed_handler, WebSocket feed consumers) legitimately run at 20-30M misses/sec. Their working set is arriving packets, which cannot be cached.

To identify a core: sudo pmu-core-explain <core>

targets.query: SELECT mean("l3_miss_avg") FROM "pcm_core" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'trading' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/ ) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "core" fill(null)

panels.title: L3 misses/sec — trading cores (role=trading)

panels.description:
L3 misses/sec on non-isolated cores (kernel work, systemd, daemons).

100K-500K misses/sec → Normal. Kernel code has poor cache locality.
<10K/sec → Core is idle.
>1M/sec sustained → Something intensive running (log rotation, backup, etc.) 

sudo Investigate with pmu-core-explain <core>

targets.query: SELECT mean("l3_miss_avg") FROM "pcm_core" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'housekeeping' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/ ) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "core" fill(null)

panels.title: L3 misses/sec — housekeeping cores (role=housekeeping)

panels.description:
L3 misses per 1000 instructions retired. Workload-normalized cache health.
Interpret by thread type (use sudo pmu-core-explain <core> to identify):

Strategy/compute cores — MPKI <0.01 is baseline. >1.0 = memory-bound, investigate.

Ingest/feed cores — MPKI 5-15 is normal. Packets cannot be cached.
Sudden jump on any core — real signal regardless of class.

targets.query: SELECT mean("l3_miss_avg") / mean("instructions_avg") * 1000 FROM "pcm_core" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'trading' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/ ) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "core" fill(null)

panels.title: MPKI — trading cores (role=trading)

panels.description:
MPKI on housekeeping cores. Baseline 0.1-0.5 — kernel code is inherently cache-unfriendly.

The 1.0 threshold line does not apply here. Watch for sudden jumps against each core's own history, not absolute values.

targets.query: SELECT mean("l3_miss_avg") / mean("instructions_avg") * 1000 FROM "pcm_core" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'housekeeping' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/ ) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval), "core" fill(null)

panels.title: MPKI — housekeeping cores (role=housekeeping)
Fleet aggregates — trading pool percentiles (min/p25/p50/p75/max across all trading cores)

panels.description:
IPC distribution across ALL trading cores in the selected hosts. Each 5-min sample produces min/p25/p50/p75/max.

min drops below 1.0 — some core has stalled, investigate outliers.
p50 drops noticeably — widespread degradation.
All lines drop together — system-wide event (thermal, IRQ storm).

targets.query: SELECT min("ipc_avg") FROM "pcm_numa" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'trading' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(null)
SELECT percentile("ipc_avg", 25) FROM "pcm_numa" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'trading' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(null)
SELECT median("ipc_avg") FROM "pcm_numa" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'trading' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(null)
SELECT percentile("ipc_avg", 75) FROM "pcm_numa" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'trading' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(null)
SELECT max("ipc_avg") FROM "pcm_numa" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'trading' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(null)

panels.title: IPC percentiles across trading pool (fleet)

panels.description:
MPKI distribution across all trading cores. Log scale, vendor-agnostic.
max line normally sits at 5-15 due to ingest cores — this is expected, not an alert.

max jumps 3x its baseline → new core became memory-bound, investigate.

p50 rises above 0.1 → widespread cache pressure on compute cores (real signal).

p95 sustained above 0.01 → multiple cores drifting toward cache pressure.

targets.query: SELECT min("l3_miss_avg") / min("instructions_avg") * 1000 FROM "pcm_core" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'trading' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(null)

SELECT percentile("l3_miss_avg", 25) / percentile("instructions_avg", 25) * 1000 FROM "pcm_core" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'trading' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(null)

SELECT percentile("l3_miss_avg", 50) / percentile("instructions_avg", 50) * 1000 FROM "pcm_core" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'trading' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(null)

SELECT percentile("l3_miss_avg", 75) / percentile("instructions_avg", 75) * 1000 FROM "pcm_core" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'trading' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(null)

SELECT max("l3_miss_avg") / max("instructions_avg") * 1000 FROM "pcm_core" WHERE ("scope" = 'core' AND "role" = 'trading' AND "host" =~ /^$host$/) AND $timeFilter GROUP BY time($__interval) fill(null)
